bug.title: /classify endpoint bypasses the LangGraph orchestrator (violates v4-043)
bug.description: Code/ConversationalUX/FindCareChat/backend/main.py:382 @app.post('/classify') handler calls _safety_service.is_emergency() and _specialty_service.find_specialty_codes() directly, bypassing the LangGraph orchestrator (_chat_graph) used by /chat. This is the parallel-path bug that lets a safety-classifier change silently break one path while the other looks fine. Manifested 2026-04-19 when the query 'I need a Shrink in DE' triggered a safety false-positive on /classify, returning {emergency: true} that the frontend mis-rendered as 'Could not identify relevant specialties.' Fix: refactor /classify to either (a) be a thin wrapper that invokes a subset of the graph (just classify + safety nodes), or (b) be deprecated with the frontend always going through /chat. Per v4-041 severity_by_environment intent: dev=critical, qa=show_stopper, prod=show_stopper.
pytest_success_criteria: /classify route handler body contains _chat_graph.invoke(...) or equivalent graph entry call
preCommitScan graph_entry_check passes for Code/ConversationalUX/FindCareChat/backend/main.py
Same query through /chat and /classify produces consistent behavior across safety + classification.
bug.reproduction: 1. POST {message: 'I need a Shrink in DE'} to https://localhost:7860/classify. 2. Observe response: {emergency: true, response: 'Call 911...'}. 3. POST same message to /chat. 4. Observe whether /chat behaves consistently (likely also false-positives via shared safety_service, but routes through the graph).
next_action: Decide refactor approach for /classify: (a) graph subset wrapper, or (b) deprecate and route frontend through /chat.

bug.title: preCommitScan has no executor for v4-043 graph-orchestration enforcement
bug.description: Engineering rule v4-043 declares enforcement type 'graph_entry_check' but preCommitScan.py + pre_deploy_rule_check.py do not yet implement that executor. Until built, v4-043 is documentation-only and new violations will land at check-in undetected. The executor needs AST-level analysis (not pure regex) to detect FastAPI/Flask route handlers whose body does not invoke a StateGraph. Per v4-041 severity_by_environment intent: dev=low, qa=critical, prod=show_stopper.
pytest_success_criteria: preCommitScan.py EXECUTORS dict has 'graph_entry_check' key
When run against a synthetic file containing a non-graph @app.post handler, the executor reports a violation
When run against the same file with a graph.invoke() call, the executor reports clean
bug.reproduction: Add a new @app.post handler that calls a service directly (bypassing any StateGraph) - commit succeeds without warning.
next_action: Implement enforce_graph_entry_check(rule_id, enforcement) in preCommitScan.py + pre_deploy_rule_check.py using ast module.

bug.title: Tracking: 20 FastAPI handlers exempted from v4-043 graph-orchestration rule (mechanical exemptions for health/splash/proxy/debug/security primitives)
bug.description:
Bookkeeping bug — not a defect. Tracks the 20 FastAPI route handlers that were marked `# graph-exempt` to clear the v4-043 pre-push scanner. The exemptions are mechanical: each handler carries no business logic that v4-043 is meant to gate (health checks, static splash pages, transfer/proxy redirects, debug endpoints, mTLS/session/Key Vault security primitives). Paired with risk_acceptance entry RA-ARCH-GRAPH-EXEMPT-001 (accepted 2026-04-19, expires 2026-12-31). Real v4-043 violations remain blocking under BUG-ARCH-GRAPH-001 (/classify and EvaluateCare scoring endpoints).

Exempted handlers:
- Code/ConversationalUX/FindCareChat/backend/main.py: health, get_session, evaluate_splash, transfer_to_findcare, evaluate_proxy, shared_splash, shared_verify_token, evaluate_verify_token, serve_index
- Code/evaluate_care/app.py: debug_verify_live, debug_bootstrap, health, splash, transfer_to_findcare, verify_token
- Code/shared_services/app.py: health, splash, transfer_to_findcare, verify_token, get_secret

Work the bug tracks: revisit each exemption when the broader graph-orchestration refactor is scheduled. For each handler, decide one of: (a) leave exempt permanently because the handler genuinely has no shared-concern surface; (b) route through a thin graph wrapper if any shared concern (audit, auth gating) becomes relevant; (c) delete the handler if it has been superseded.
pytest_success_criteria: Each of the 20 exempted handlers has been re-reviewed during the scheduled graph-orchestration refactor.
For each handler, a disposition decision (leave exempt / wrap in graph / delete) is recorded.
RA-ARCH-GRAPH-EXEMPT-001 is closed or renewed based on the review outcome.
bug.reproduction: Run `python Code/Shared/ops/tools/pre_deploy_rule_check.py findcare`. The 20 handlers listed in the description are skipped by the v4-043 graph_entry_check executor because each carries an inline `# graph-exempt: <reason>; per BUG-ARCH-GRAPH-EXEMPT-001` comment within the 4 lines preceding the function def. Removing the comment from any one would cause that handler to re-enter the scanner's violation list.
next_action: Schedule alongside BUG-ARCH-GRAPH-001 graph-orchestration refactor work; revisit every exempted handler at that time.

bug.title: Prime rule (no misrepresentation) lives only in CLAUDE.md, has no runtime enforcement point
bug.description: Claude does not obey the prime objective in CLAUDE.md. The rule lives only in CLAUDE.md, has no entry in engineering_rules.json, and no hook enforcement. This work fixes that gap.
pytest_success_criteria: engineering_rules.json contains a rule entry whose text matches the prime rule from CLAUDE.md verbatim
That rule entry has at least two enforcement entries: prompt_verify_directive (UserPromptSubmit) and response_claim_audit (Stop)
AnthropicsClaudeCodeHookManager implements enforce_prompt_verify_directive and enforce_response_claim_audit
Pytest for prompt_verify_directive: feeding a high-risk prompt injects the verification directive; feeding a benign prompt does not
Pytest for response_claim_audit: a response with definitive external-system claims AND no Read/Grep/Bash/WebFetch tool calls this turn produces a violation record
CLAUDE.md no longer contains the prime-rule preamble; it points to the rule ID instead

bug.title: 3 backend files violate EPIC-008-F-004-S-001-REQ-T-001 standard-ports rule
bug.description: EPIC-008-F-004-S-001-REQ-T-001 requires standard ports 80, 443, 7860, 8001, 8002 across all environments. Three backend files reference non-standard ports as defaults or in CORS allow_origins: (1) Code/ConversationalUX/FindCareChat/backend/main.py:589 defaults EVALCARE_URL to https://localhost:8081 (Caddy mTLS port that does not exist in the local deploy and is not in the standard set); (2) Code/evaluate_care/app.py:89-90 lists https://localhost:3000 and https://localhost:8080 in CORS allow_origins; (3) Code/shared_services/app.py:87-88 lists https://localhost:3000, https://localhost:8080, https://localhost:8081. bug.title: Right-panel /verify-token call goes to FindCare (proxy), not directly to the cold-button service
bug.description: Per EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-T-007 the browser MUST call the cold-button service's /verify-token endpoint directly. Today Website/index.html openSharedServices() and openEvaluateCare() both POST /shared/verify-token and /evaluate/verify-token to FindCare (apiBase + '/shared/verify-token' and apiBase + '/evaluate/verify-token'). FindCare then proxies the call server-side via requests.post to the peer service. The right panel renders the result, but the operator cannot independently verify (via DevTools Network tab or smoke test) that the cold-button service actually verified the token — all visible HTTP traffic terminates at FindCare. This is a validation gap as well as an architectural mismatch with the per-owner banner refresh (EPIC-008-F-004-S-004-REQ-B-007) and the Env/Time token rows (EPIC-002-F-001-S-012-REQ-B-009) which already report the active service.

bug.title: V17 §4.9.3 step 3 mandates URL-pattern resolver that crashes on JSON Schema meta-schema URL
bug.description: V17 §4.9.3 step 3 stipulated that the worker resolve a JSON file's $schema URL by stripping the prefix `https://(dev|qa|)?chathealthy.ai/schemas/` and treating the suffix as a filename under Website/schemas/. That design is non-functional whenever a JSON file declares a $schema URL outside the chathealthy.ai pattern — most importantly, schema files themselves declare `$schema = https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema` (the JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema). Under V17, the URL-pattern resolver fails on those files and raises WorkerInternalError, which the worker maps to exit 5 and blocks pre-commit. The defect is in V17 itself, not the implementation: the implementation was honoring V17 §4.9.3 step 3 as written. Resolution: V18 §4.9.3 replaces the URL-pattern resolver with web fetch (HTTP GET, 5s timeout, per-run cache) and adds a single carve-out for the JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema (whose URL is contractually frozen by the spec). Unreachable URLs become per-file ViolationRecords, never WorkerInternalError. See V18 §4.9.3.1 for the carve-out policy and V18 Table 12 for the resolution mechanism.
bug.reproduction: Under V17: stage Website/schemas/EngineeringRulesSchema.json; attempt git commit; pre-commit's CHECK 11 invokes the manager which dispatches scan_files_enforcement_worker; the worker reads $schema = https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema; the V17 URL-pattern resolver cannot map that URL to a Website/schemas/<file>.json path; the worker raises WorkerInternalError, exits 5, and the commit is blocked.
bug.fix: Resolved by V19 §4.9.3 / §4.9.3.1 carve-out policy. ScanFilesEnforcementWorker._load_frozen_external_schemas() (architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/scan_files_enforcement_worker.py) builds a {url: schema} carve-out map at __init__ that maps the JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema URL (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema) to the local copy at Website/schemas/standard/json-schema-2020-12-meta.json. _resolve_schema() consults the carve-out before any web fetch, so schema files declaring the meta-schema URL no longer trigger a URL-pattern lookup and never raise WorkerInternalError. The V17 URL-pattern resolver has been removed.

bug.title: _validate_json conflates schema loading, file parsing, and validation; not compliant with single-responsibility principle implicit in BR-11/TR-12
bug.description: V17 BR-11 / TR-12 stipulate that JSON validation is performed by jsonschema.Draft202012Validator against the schema declared in $schema. The function _validate_json was implemented as an orchestrator that also (a) parses the file as JSON and (b) loads the schema via inline URL resolution. This violates single-responsibility and gives the function room to invent constraints. Result: SCOPES has no `\.json$` allowed_pattern for _validate_json, the function runs on Python and shell files, json.load() raises JSONDecodeError, and 5 spurious 'invalid JSON' violations are emitted on non-JSON files. Refactor: _validate_json must do nothing but call the standard library validator. Schema loading moves to __init__ (registry built once). File parsing and schema lookup move to run().
bug.reproduction: Stage any non-JSON file (e.g., Code/DataPipelines/prescriber_evaluate_care_pipeline.py); attempt git commit; the worker emits a 'invalid JSON: Expecting value at line 1 col 1' violation.
bug.fix: Resolved by SRP refactor of _validate_json in V19. ScanFilesEnforcementWorker._validate_json (architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/scan_files_enforcement_worker.py) is now a 4-line wrapper that does only `return list(jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(schema).iter_errors(data))`. File parsing moved to _load_data, schema resolution moved to _resolve_schema (carve-out -> per-run cache -> HTTP GET), and orchestration moved to _check_one_file_json. The worker's enforcement entry now carries an `["_validate_json", "allowed_pattern", ["\\.json$"]]` row gating the validator to JSON files only, so non-JSON files no longer enter the validator path.
